sections.h2: What the Athens County Recorder handles
sections.html:
The recorder keeps the public land records. If a paper transfers any interest in land, it is recorded here, as are DD214 military discharge papers and financing statements that create a lien on real property. The office opens at eight on weekdays, closes at four, and is shut on weekends.

Real property records run from 1790 to the present, with alphabetical indices covering the same span. Staff can direct you to records, though they do not perform title searches. Ownership history is on the AvaWeb portal, free to view and print.

Basic recording is $34.00 for pages one and two, $8.00 for every printed page after that, and $4.00 per marginal notation. Those totals come from ORC 317.32, which splits each into halves: a $17 base fee plus a $17 housing trust fund fee on the first two pages, and $4 plus $4 on each later page.

A county may also add a document preservation surcharge, capped at $5 by statute. Ask the recorder whether it applies before you send payment.

sections.h2: Why a deed may be rejected or surcharged
sections.html:
Ohio House Bill 525, effective July 1, 2009, set standardization rules that nearly all recorded documents must meet. Papers that fall short are still accepted, for an extra $20.00. Documents also have to be drafted and signed as Ohio law requires, so use a preparer who knows the state's rules.

  • Count your pages before mailing a check, because pages set the fee.
  • If you are unsure of the total, phone the office. Its own fee list controls.
  • Direct formatting questions to the recorder. A template is on the Ohio Recorders' Association site.

The recorder does not collect the transfer charge. That belongs to the auditor. ORC 319.202 has the buyer file a statement of value before the auditor endorses the deed, and ORC 319.54(G)(3) sets the charge at a $1 floor or 10 cents per $100 of value (or fraction), whichever is higher. The seller pays it, plus any Chapter 322 county transfer tax.

Certain transfers owe nothing, among them gifts between spouses, gifts from parent to child, delinquent-tax sales and transfers to the trustee of a revocable trust. Call the Athens County auditor at 740-592-3223 to learn whether one fits your deed.

sections.h2: Documents in a typical house sale
sections.html:
A typical sale involves a deed and, if the seller had a loan, a mortgage release. Occasionally a power of attorney or an affidavit about a deceased owner joins them. Every one is recorded separately and priced by page.

  • The deed moving title from seller to buyer, either warranty or fiduciary.
  • A mortgage release, filed once the lender is paid at closing.
  • An affidavit or court certificate if an estate is the seller.

Condition, tenants or probate history do not stop an as-is sale, and the title steps are unchanged. Title companies confirm the chain of ownership in the recorder's index.

One sale involves several offices, and visiting the wrong one costs a trip. The recorder gets deeds and mortgage releases. At the auditor you file the statement of value and pay the conveyance fee, and the homestead and owner-occupancy records live there. The treasurer handles tax payments and payoffs.

  • Recorder: records the deed, charges per page, and holds the index from 1790.
  • Auditor: endorses the conveyance and files the statement of value required by ORC 319.202.
  • Treasurer: tax bills, payments and payment plans.

Only UCC filings tied to real estate have gone to the county since July 1, 2001. Other personal property filings go to the Ohio Secretary of State, so a lien on equipment or inventory will not appear in the county index.

The statute is the ceiling for what every Ohio recorder charges, and Athens County's figures follow it. Certifying a copy runs $1 base plus $1 housing trust fund per page, with 50 cents plus 50 cents when the seal is required. A marginal reference made by separate instrument is $2 plus $2.

Local fax or electronic transmission is one dollar plus one dollar per page, and long-distance fax is two dollars plus two dollars per page. Instruments filed by a county land reutilization corporation are exempt. The county quotes its own totals for copies, so treat its listing as the number that controls and call to confirm.

A few more charges matter to lenders and title agents. A UCC termination is $12.00, and a search costs $20.00 plus $2.00 for each page of copies requested. If a closing depends on an exact total, confirm by phone.

sections.h2: Look up your records before you sell
sections.html:
Open AvaWeb, the free online land record search, and print the latest deed on file. The auditor's website shows current parcel data, and recorder staff can name the right index volume for older records. Plain copies run $2.00 a page, and certified copies add a $1.00 certification.

Check that the name on the deed matches the name you will sign with, and that any old mortgage shows a release. Clearing a gap now is cheaper than clearing it at closing, and a cash buyer will run the same title search a lender would.

sections.h2: Recording a deed step by step
sections.html:
Have the deed prepared to Ohio's formatting standards, and count its pages so you know the fee. Take it to the auditor for the statement of value and endorsement, and pay the conveyance fee there. Then bring the endorsed deed to the recorder with payment, for example $34.00 for a two-page deed. If the seller had a mortgage, the lender's release goes in as its own recording. The recorder indexes everything, and that index is what the next title search will read.

Most sellers never do this personally, because the title company or closing agent files the paperwork. If you are handling it yourself, phone the recorder first, confirm the current fees, and ask whether anything about your document looks nonstandard.

A cash buyer removes the lender, so there is no new mortgage to record and the closing can move faster. The seller's side stays the same. Any old mortgage still needs its release recorded, the auditor still takes the statement of value, and the treasurer still supplies a tax payoff. The deed is recorded at the same page-based fee. If you want the deal done quickly, getting the payoff and the deed formatting right in advance is what saves the time.
Athens County had 62,431 people in 2020, with a 2025 estimate of 63,197. About 54.4% of occupied homes are owner-occupied and 45.6% are rented, so many deeds in the county involve rental property.

faqs.q: What are the Athens County Recorder's hours?
What fees apply when Athens County records my deed?
faqs.a: The county charges $34.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page added. A nonstandard document can be recorded for $20.00 more.

faqs.q: Can I search Athens County land records online?
faqs.a: Yes, through AvaWeb, where documents can be viewed and printed free. Records reach back to 1790.

faqs.q: Does the recorder bill the conveyance fee?
faqs.a: No, the county auditor does. The conveyance fee is $1 or 10 cents per $100 of value or fraction, whichever is higher, plus any Chapter 322 county tax.

faqs.q: How much is a certified copy?
faqs.a: The county charges $2.00 per page plus $1.00 for certification. Plain copies cost $2.00 a page.
